hook.line: Mariana writes for a newspaper, and newspapers love *tras*. It is the formal way to say "after", and you will read it constantly even if you rarely say it.
hook.es: Tras hablar con Altamira, Yesid se fue a casa.
hook.en: After talking to Altamira, Yesid went home.

examples.es: Tras firmar el acuerdo, el ministro habló con la prensa.
examples.en: After signing the agreement, the minister spoke to the press.

examples.es: Tras la reunión, se suspendió el paro.
examples.en: After the meeting, the strike was called off.

examples.es: Tras hablar con el abogado, Tomás llamó a Vale.
examples.en: After talking to the lawyer, Tomás called Vale.

examples.es: Yesid salió tras escuchar la oferta.
examples.en: Yesid left after hearing the offer.

examples.es: Tras varios meses de silencio, Yesid contó la verdad.
examples.en: After several months of silence, Yesid told the truth.

examples.es: Tras comer, Hernando pidió un tinto.
examples.en: After eating, Hernando ordered a black coffee.

rule:
*Tras* means "after", but in writing and the news. It takes a noun (*tras la reunión*) or an infinitive (*tras firmar*).

Spanish has no "-ing" here: English "after signing" is *tras firmar*, never *tras firmando*.

The person who does both actions is usually the same, and is named after the comma.

Say it as *tras*, not *tras de*. In conversation, most people prefer *después de*: *después de comer*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a temporal preposition with an infinitive. It is the same idea as *después de*, in a written register.

readAndPick.es: Tras firmar el acuerdo, el ministro habló con la prensa.
options: Before signing the agreement, the minister spoke to the press.
After signing the agreement, the minister spoke to the press.
Instead of signing the agreement, the minister spoke to the press.

readAndPick.es: Tras la reunión, se suspendió el paro.
options: The strike was called off before the meeting.
The strike was called off during the meeting.
The strike was called off after the meeting.

readAndPick.es: Yesid salió tras escuchar la oferta.
options: Yesid left after hearing the offer.
Yesid left to hear the offer.
Yesid left without hearing the offer.
After signing, he read everything.
Before signing, he read everything.
Instead of signing, he read everything.

readAndPick.es: Tras comer, Hernando pidió un tinto.
options: While eating, Hernando ordered a black coffee.
Before eating, Hernando ordered a black coffee.
After eating, Hernando ordered a black coffee.

readAndPick.es: Tras varios meses de silencio, Yesid contó la verdad.
options: After several months of silence, Yesid told the truth.
Despite several months of silence, Yesid told the truth.
Before several months of silence, Yesid told the truth.
After talking to her, I left.
After talking to her, they left.
After talking to her, we left.

readAndPick.es: Tras la asamblea, nadie quiso comentar.
options: Before the assembly, nobody wanted to comment.
After the assembly, nobody wanted to comment.
During the assembly, nobody wanted to comment.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tras* or *antes de* (the sentence means "after"): ___ hablar con Vale, Tomás se fue. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Tras hablar con Vale, Tomás se fue.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *firmar* or *firmando*: Tras ___ el acuerdo, salió. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: After *tras*, Spanish uses the infinitive, not the *-ando* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Use *tras*: After the meeting, nobody spoke.
yourTurn.why: *Tras* plus a noun works like "after" plus a noun.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: After eating, Hernando ordered a black coffee.
yourTurn.answer: Tras comer, Hernando pidió un tinto.
accept: Tras comer, Hernando pidió un café.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal with *tras*: *Después de escuchar la oferta, Yesid se fue.*
yourTurn.answer: Tras escuchar la oferta, Yesid se fue.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it the everyday way, with *después de*: *Tras la reunión, hablé con ella.*
yourTurn.answer: Después de la reunión, hablé con ella.
accept: Después de la reunión hablé con ella.
yourTurn.why: In conversation *después de* is the usual choice.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, using *tras* (the lawyer is a man): After talking to the lawyer, we called Vale.
yourTurn.answer: Tras hablar con el abogado, llamamos a Vale.
yourTurn.why: The doers are named after the comma: *llamamos* tells you it was "we".

pitfalls.why: Almost. English "after signing" uses the infinitive in Spanish, not the *-ando* form.
Almost. *Tras* takes a noun or an infinitive, not a *que* clause.

personal: Say what you did after a recent meeting or meal, in writing style: *Tras…, yo…*
